From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Short remit window & AP checklist — need confirmation for INV-9204

Hi Alicia / Tom,

Hope you're both well. Quick follow-up on INV-9204 (due 09/18) — AP reached out this morning asking for a short remit plan so we can lock the settlement window. To avoid any last-minute routing issues, can you confirm the following by EOD Monday?

- Preferred primary route: ACH (US) or virtual card?
- If ACH: bank name, routing, account last 4 digits and whether the payment goes to Helion US entity (for tax matching).
- If virtual card: is there a spend cap or single-charge limit we should split around?
- Any outstanding credits to net against INV-9204 (please attach remittance advice).

I've attached the invoice and our standard ACH authorization form for your AP team to complete. If ACH is doable, we can schedule payment on 09/18 and avoid a virtual-card split. If you prefer splitting, we can accept ACH for an agreed portion and virtual card for the remainder — please indicate amounts.

AP checklist (for quick copy/paste to your team):
1) Confirm route and provide bank or card payment contact.
2) Send W9 or VAT residency doc if your accounting requires it.
3) Confirm any prior-credit amount to net.

Thanks — we want to make this painless on your side so funds clear inside your payroll window.

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: INV-9204.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks Grace — quick answers from our AP side below.

We can do ACH for the majority but need to net an outstanding credit of $5,420 from invoice INV-9112 (credit memo attached internally). That would leave a remaining balance of $84,180 on INV-9204. Our AP policy caps single virtual-card charges at $50k; above that we need split approval.

Proposed split: ACH for $80k on 09/18, virtual card for the remaining $9,600 (the virtual-card fee will be on us). If that works, we'll complete your ACH authorization and attach our W9.

I've attached our vendor form and the remittance note for INV-9112. Can you confirm whether Redwood allows netting internal credits at signing (we require a written confirmation from vendor)? If so, we'll route ACH as proposed.

Regards,
Alicia Moreno
Head of Finance Operations | Helion AI
[Attachment: helion_vendor_remit.pdf (PDF)]

Grace / Marissa,

Short answer: we can allow netting of credits against current invoices provided the credit memo comes from the same legal entity and there's a clear remittance note (Helion's remittance doc looks fine). A couple of governance notes for finance:

- We need a signed confirmation in an email thread (Alicia's message counts) and the credit memo attached to their payment instruction.
- If they pay via virtual card for a portion, record the card fee as an expense offset (they offered to cover it — fine).

Confirming Redwood accepts the $5,420 credit memo from INV-9112 to be netted against INV-9204, provided Helion's AP includes the credit memo on the wire/virtual-card remittance advice. Per Ben's note, please attach your W9 with the ACH instruction.

We agree to the proposed routing plan:
- ACH (US) for $80,000 scheduled 2027-09-18
- Virtual card for $9,600 to cover the balance; Helion will absorb any card processing fees

Next steps for Helion AP:
1) Complete and return the signed ACH authorization (attached).
2) Upload W9 to the DocuSign link here: https://www.docusign.com/HLN/INV-9204/authorize
3) Include the INV-9112 credit memo in the payment remittance field or attach to the wire advice.

I've attached our signed ACH authorization form (returned). Once I see the W9 and remittance thread, I'll mark the invoice settled on our side and schedule reconciliation. If the virtual-card confirmation will be later than EOD Wednesday, ping me and we'll schedule a small buffer.

Thanks — appreciate the responsiveness.
